page: Amazon Web Services vt1.24xlarge is an accelerated computing instance engineered primarily for video transcoding and media processing workflows. Powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance runs on an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. It provides 96 vCPUs derived from 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The system incorporates 192.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, matching a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. A key architectural characteristic of vt1.24xlarge is the inclusion of 8 Xilinx U30 media accelerator cards offering a total of 192 GB of dedicated accelerator VRAM. There is no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions, while baseline network throughput is rated at 25 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate a clear separation between aggregate multi-threaded execution and individual core throughput. In synthetic CPU evaluations, the platform demonstrates top-tier multi-core capability, recording 80,289.99 in stress-ng multi-core and 53,507.92 in PassMark overall CPU, bolstered by strong extended instruction execution (73,176.36) and hardware-accelerated encryption (36,526.49). Memory throughput is exceptionally high, with uncached read operations achieving 214.18 GB/sec and uncached writes reaching 94.04 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core metrics fall into the bottom 25th percentile, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,146.0 and stress-ng single-core performance of 1,284.09. Similarly, single-threaded compression tests such as gzip (21.93 GB/sec) and bzip3 (8.51 GB/sec) reflect weak single-thread performance.

The instance delivers strong capabilities in high-concurrency memory-bound environments, achieving 73.73 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 44.61 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. However, its specialized Xilinx U30 ASICs are configured for video pipelines rather than general-purpose matrix compute. Consequently, CPU-driven LLM inference benchmarks reflect weak generation performance, dropping to 31.9 tokens/sec on small (135M) models and 5.2 tokens/sec on medium (7B) models, placing it in the bottom 10th percentile for language model token generation.

The hardware configuration provides favorable resource density for high-throughput video transcoding clusters and highly parallel I/O tasks. Because storage relies strictly on external networks and single-threaded performance is modest, workloads requiring local scratch disks or high sequential single-thread speed will face performance tradeoffs. The instance is suited for multi-stream live video encoding, transcoded media distribution, concurrent streaming ingestion, and high-throughput in-memory caching fleets.

Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it features an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor delivering 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores at 2.5 GHz, paired with 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory. Hardware acceleration is provided by 8 Xilinx U30 media processors totaling 192 GB of VRAM. It includes 25 Gbps baseline networking and has no local storage. Benchmark data reflects high aggregate multi-core throughput (stress-ng multi-core at 80,289.99) and robust uncached memory reads of 214.18 GB/sec, alongside top-tier Redis throughput of 73.73 million operations/sec. In contrast, single-thread compute and LLM text generation metrics sit in the lowest percentiles. vt1.24xlarge is optimized for live video encoding, high-stream transcoding, and memory-bound caching workloads.
